title: "10 · Centrality and export"
execute:

---

Betweenness on a street network concentrates: the busiest 5 % of junctions carry
23 % of it, and of streets, 26 %. The notebook computes it on intersections and,
through the line graph, on the streets themselves, which is the reading most
urban analysis wants.

It also closes the suite by asking what survives leaving it. Of eight export
routes tabulated, every GraphML, GEXF and JSON export comes out **undirected**
regardless of the graph, one route loses 12 of 375 segments to a silent default,
another turns every attribute into a string, and only the GeoPackage round trip
returns float64 values unchanged.

The finding easiest to miss: `Use Length Weight` does nothing at all while
`Use Rustworkx (Fast)` is ticked, because the fast path loads the lengths and
then calls a function that takes no weight argument. The weighted answer, which
moves three of the top five junctions, sits behind what reads as a performance
switch.
